section-226F-1.TO: exercise a power to examine a third party bulk personal dataset
section-226F-1.UNLESS: the examination of the dataset is authorised by a third party BPD warrant

section-226F-3.TO: authorise the examination of a bulk personal dataset— (a) the content of which may vary from time to time, or (b) that does not exist at the time of the issue of the warrant

section-226G-1.FOR: The head of an intelligence service, or a person acting on their behalf
section-226G-1.TO: apply to the Secretary of State for a third party BPD warrant

section-226G-2.TO: include a general description of the bulk personal dataset (or datasets) to which the application relates

section-226G-3.TO: include a statement to that effect
section-226G-3.WHERE: the person making the application knows that subsection (6) applies to any bulk personal dataset to which the application relates

section-226G-4.IF: — (a) the Secretary of State considers that the warrant is necessary— (i) in the interests of national security, (ii) for the purposes of preventing or detecting serious crime, or (iii) in the interests of the economic well-being of the United Kingdom so far as those interests are also relevant to the interests of national security, (b) the Secretary of State considers that the conduct authorised by the warrant is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by the conduct, (c) the Secretary of State considers that the arrangements made by the intelligence service for examining the bulk personal dataset (or datasets) to which the application relates are satisfactory, and (d) except where the Secretary of State considers that there is an urgent need to issue the warrant, the decision to issue the warrant has been approved by a Judicial Commissioner

section-226G-9.FOR: An application for a third party BPD warrant
section-226G-9.TO: be made on behalf of the head of an intelligence service
section-226G-9.ONLY BY: a person holding office under the Crown

section-226GA-1.TO: review the Secretary of State’s conclusions as to the following matters— (a) whether the warrant is necessary on grounds falling within section 226G (4) (a), and (b) whether the conduct that would be authorised by the warrant is proportionate to what is sought to be achieved by that conduct
section-226GA-1.IN: deciding whether to approve a decision to issue a third party BPD warrant

section-226GA-2.TO: — (a) apply the same principles as would be applied by a court on an application for judicial review, and (b) consider the matters referred to in subsection (1) with a sufficient degree of care as to ensure that the Judicial Commissioner complies with the duties imposed by section 2 (general duties in relation to privacy)

section-226GA-3.TO: give the Secretary of State written reasons for the refusal
section-226GA-3.WHERE: the Judicial Commissioner refuses to approve a decision to issue a third party BPD warrant

section-226GA-4.TO: ask the Investigatory Powers Commissioner to decide whether to approve the decision to issue the warrant
section-226GA-4.WHERE: a Judicial Commissioner, other than the Investigatory Powers Commissioner, refuses to approve a decision to issue a third party BPD warrant

section-226GB-2.TO: inform a Judicial Commissioner that it has been issued

section-226GB-3.TO: — (a) decide whether to approve the decision to issue the warrant, and (b) notify the Secretary of State of the Judicial Commissioner’s decision
section-226GB-3.BEFORE: the end of the relevant period

section-226GB-6.FOR: The head of the intelligence service to whom the warrant was addressed
section-226GB-6.TO: secure that anything in the process of being done in reliance on the warrant stops as soon as possible

section-226GC-1.FOR: The decision to issue a third party BPD warrant
section-226GC-1.TO: be taken personally by the Secretary of State

section-226GC-2.TO: be signed by the Secretary of State

section-226GC-3.TO: be signed by a senior official designated by the Secretary of State for that purpose
section-226GC-3.IF: it is not reasonably practicable for the warrant to be signed by the Secretary of State

section-226GC-4.TO: contain a statement that— (a) it is not reasonably practicable for the warrant to be signed by the Secretary of State, and (b) the Secretary of State has personally and expressly authorised the issue of the warrant

section-226HA-1.TO: be renewed by an instrument issued by the Secretary of State
section-226HA-1.AT: any time during the renewal period

section-226HA-4.FOR: The decision to renew a third party BPD warrant
section-226HA-4.TO: be taken personally by the Secretary of State
be signed by the Secretary of State

section-226HB-1.FOR: The Secretary of State, or a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State
section-226HB-1.TO: cancel a third party BPD warrant

section-226HB-2.FOR: the Secretary of State, or a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State
section-226HB-2.TO: cancel a third party BPD warrant
section-226HB-2.IF: the person considers that any of the cancellation conditions are met in relation to the warrant

section-226HC-2.FOR: The head of the intelligence service to whom the warrant was addressed
section-226HC-2.TO: secure that anything in the process of being done in reliance on the warrant stops as soon as possible

section-226I-2.FOR: The head of the intelligence service, or a person acting on their behalf
section-226I-2.TO: carry out an initial inspection of the contents of the set for the purpose of deciding whether, if the intelligence service were to examine it after that initial inspection— (a) the intelligence service would be examining a third party bulk personal dataset (see section  226E) , and (b) such examination would be necessary and proportionate in all the circumstances

section-226I-4.FOR: The head of the intelligence service, or a person acting on their behalf
section-226I-4.TO: decide whether to examine the third party bulk personal dataset

section-226I-4.FOR: The head of the intelligence service, or a person acting on their behalf
section-226I-4.TO: apply for a third party BPD warrant

section-226I-7.FOR: only a person holding office under the Crown
section-226I-7.TO: For the purposes of this section, act on behalf of the head of an intelligence service

section-226IA-1.TO: ensure that arrangements are in force for securing that any examination of data contained in the dataset is necessary and proportionate in all the circumstances
section-226IA-1.IN RELATION TO: every third party BPD warrant which authorises the examination of a bulk personal dataset

section-226IA-2.TO: have regard to the information that is reasonably available to the intelligence services in relation to the examination of such data

section-226IB-2.TO: be examined using the relevant criteria
section-226IB-2.IF: the relevant criteria are referable to an individual known to be in the British Islands at the time of the examination
section-226IB-2.ONLY IF: the Secretary of State has approved the use of those criteria

section-226IB-3.TO: be examined using the relevant criteria
section-226IB-3.ONLY IF: a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State has approved the use of those criteria

section-226IB-4.TO: give approval for the purposes of subsection (2)
section-226IB-4.ONLY WITH: the approval of a Judicial Commissioner

section-226IB-5.ONLY IF: where subsection (1)(a) applies, the Secretary of State or (as the case may be) the senior official considers that there are exceptional and compelling circumstances that make it necessary to authorise the use of the relevant criteria

section-226IB-6.FOR: the Secretary of State or (as the case may be) the senior official
section-226IB-6.TO: have regard to the public interest in the confidentiality of items subject to legal privilege
section-226IB-6.IN: deciding whether to give an approval under subsection (2) or (3) in a case where subsection (1) (a) applies

section-226IB-8.TO: — (a) apply the same principles as would be applied by a court on an application for judicial review, and (b) consider the matter with a sufficient degree of care as to ensure that the Judicial Commissioner complies with the duties imposed by section 2 (general duties in relation to privacy)
section-226IB-8.IN: deciding whether to give approval for the purposes of subsection (4)

section-226IB-10.TO: be examined using the relevant criteria
section-226IB-10.IF: the relevant criteria are referable to an individual known to be in the British Islands at the time of the examination
section-226IB-10.ONLY IF: the Secretary of State has approved the use of those criteria

section-226IB-11.TO: be examined using the relevant criteria
section-226IB-11.ONLY IF: a senior official acting on behalf of the Secretary of State has approved the use of those criteria

section-226IB-12.ONLY IF: the Secretary of State or (as the case may be) the senior official considers that the targeted data or the underlying material is likely to be data or underlying material created or held with the intention of furthering a criminal purpose

section-226IC-2.FOR: The person to whom the third party BPD warrant (mentioned in subsection (1)(a)) is addressed
section-226IC-2.AS SOON AS: reasonably practicable after retaining the item

section-226IC-3.TO: — (a) direct that the item is destroyed, or (b) impose one or more conditions as to the use or retention of that item
section-226IC-3.UNLESS: the Commissioner considers that subsection (5) applies to the item

section-226IC-4.TO: impose such conditions under subsection (3)(b) as the Commissioner considers necessary for the purpose of protecting the public interest in the confidentiality of items subject to legal privilege
section-226IC-4.IF: the Commissioner considers that subsection (5) applies to the item

section-226IC-6.TO: require an affected party to make representations about how the Commissioner should exercise any function under subsection (3)
have regard to any such representations made by an affected party (whether or not as a result of a requirement imposed under paragraph (a))

section-226ID-1.TO: — (a) examine, in reliance on a third party BPD warrant, any data contained in a third party bulk personal dataset, (b) know or believe that the examination of that data is in breach of the requirement specified in subsection (2), and (c) deliberately examine that data in breach of that requirement

section-226ID-4.FOR: proceedings for any offence which is an offence by virtue of this section
section-226ID-4.TO: be instituted— (a) in England and Wales, except by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions; (b) in Northern Ireland, except by or with the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions for Northern Ireland
